FIB_PLUS	<p>4688_f3f5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #556608;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #556608;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #556608;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #06678a;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #06678a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #06678a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2f4b;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9f2f4b;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2f4b;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jty, +++, jty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e5500;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7e5500;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e5500;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6c65;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #0b6c65;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6c65;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #693fbd;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #693fbd;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e5500;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7e5500;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e5500;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f4e;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006f4e;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3f52bc;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3f52bc;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3f52bc;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ace, +++, ace"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8d4a0f;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8d4a0f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d4a0f;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6e29;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2b6e29;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6e29;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3f52bc;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3f52bc;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5e00;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6d5e00;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5e00;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a77;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a77;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a77;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823998;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #823998;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5e00;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6d5e00;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5e00;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6c65;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #0b6c65;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6c65;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3f52bc;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3f52bc;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3f52bc;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fhm, +++, fhm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8d4a0f;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8d4a0f;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d4a0f;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6e29;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #2b6e29;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype.
